description: Model coordinator configuration for dual-model routing and task classification

tiers._comment: Version SSOT. Route phase/slice complexity -> tier -> concrete current model id. When a new model version ships, bump the id HERE only; downstream pools (remote_agents.py, delegate-to-gemini) should read these ids rather than hardcoding their own. Prevents the drift where pools stay pinned to superseded versions.

anthropic._comment: claude-fable-5-1 (Mythos-class tier, above Opus) is the flagship AND creative lane — most capable generally-available Claude. Opus 5.5 = deep fallback when Fable is unavailable; Sonnet 5.5 = balanced (default Claude implementer); Haiku 5.5 = fast. Behavioral parity contract for ALL lanes (any provider): .agent/FABLE-PARITY-CONTRACT.md.

google._comment: Google Gemini direct (generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai) via the antigravity wrapper -> switchboard -> Gemini backend; NOT OpenRouter (unused). LATEST ids: gemini-3.8-flash (default GA flagship+balanced — most intelligent Flash, long-horizon SWE/agents), gemini-3.5-flash-lite (fast, ultra-efficient/cost-sensitive high-volume), gemini-3.1-pro-preview (deep — advanced reasoning, complex science/coding; PREVIEW ONLY, not GA, so it is the opt-in deep tier rather than the default flagship). gemini-3.5-flash is now legacy-baseline (see baseline_fallback). Baseline fallback ids: gemini-3.5-flash, gemini-3.5-flash-lite (legacy-baseline; 2.x line is limited-access per provider docs). EFFORT (OPTIONAL, remote-native): the *_thinking_level values below are Google's native reasoning-depth control (thinking_level preset minimal|low|medium|high, or thinking_config.thinking_budget int; Vertex thinkingConfig.thinkingBudget). They tune remote reasoning DEPTH only — they are NOT defensive throttles. The remote lane scales to native API ceilings (large context, high concurrency, fast gen); do NOT apply the local Qwen ceilings (enable_thinking=false / thinking_budget~200) here. /v1beta/openai does NOT support OpenAI reasoning_effort. Default lane = gemini-3.8-flash; complex/critical deep opt-in = gemini-3.1-pro-preview (preview). gemini-3.8-flash ships in THREE reasoning-effort levels (low|medium|high via thinking_level) — see `gemini_3_8_flash_efforts` below for per-level capabilities + best-uses (low=fast agentic/IDE loops, medium=balanced default, high=cheaper deep-reasoning pass below the 3.1-pro-preview architect tier).

gemini_3_8_flash_efforts._comment: Gemini 3.8 Flash at Google's three native reasoning-effort levels (refreshed 2026-09-25 from gemini-3.5-flash). SAME model id `gemini-3.8-flash`; the level tunes reasoning DEPTH only via thinking_level (remote-native, NOT a defensive throttle — do not apply local Qwen ceilings). Choose by task shape, not task size. These back the balanced lane and give a cheaper high-reasoning step below the gemini-3.1-pro-preview architect tier.

low.best_use: Low-latency, high-concurrency coding loops and interactive iteration where speed beats depth; light triage above gemini-3.5-flash-lite.

medium.best_use: Default balanced lane — general implementation slices, standard multi-step agentic work, most day-to-day tasks.

capabilities: deeper reasoning on the fast tier
review-grade analysis short of the pro architect tier
high.best_use: Complex/critical work needing more reasoning but not the gemini-3.1-pro-preview architect tier; a cost-efficient high-reasoning pass for reviews and multi-file refactors.

gemini_lane._comment: Gemini CLI lane (scripts/ai/delegate-to-gemini, OAuth, no API keys). SSOT for ids served by `gemini models` on 2026-11-19 (Gemini CLI 1.5.12), their roles and probe results; scripts read default/fallback/required_id_prefix from here. Independence guard: the lane refuses any id not starting with required_id_prefix (claude-*, gpt-* are also listed by the CLI but are not Gemini models: a Gemini review of Claude-authored work would be a self-review and gpt-oss overlaps the Codex lane). Evidence: docs/harness-first/evidence/2026-11-19-gemini-model-roster.md. Unlike the direct-API tiers above, this lane's ids are the CLI's, not generativelanguage.googleapis.com ids.

openai._comment: OpenAI GPT-6 family (refreshed 2026-09-25 from gpt-5.5). flagship=gpt-6.2-astra (flagship reasoning/coding), balanced=gpt-6.2-sol (balanced coding/agentic), fast=gpt-6-luna (efficient/high-volume). Specialized gpt-5.6-cyber (vuln research) is available but NOT wired into a routing tier here.

local._comment: Local Qwen (single slot, SWB_LOCAL_CONCURRENCY=1, ~1-3.45 tok/s on Renoir APU / 27GB RAM). DEFENSIVE CEILINGS APPLY HERE ONLY: switchboard injects enable_thinking=false (in chat_template_kwargs) and a small local thinking_budget (~200) to prevent a single unbounded thinking loop from locking the harness ~40min or ballooning the KV cache into a GPU OOM. These ceilings must NEVER be applied to remote lanes.

tier_routing._comment: Maps task/phase/slice complexity to a tier. Each provider resolves the tier to its concrete model id via `tiers`. complexity is set by the coordinator's intent classifier (trivial|simple|medium|complex|critical) or explicitly per phase.
